article.Citation: Rydzynski Z, Gruszczynski W. Treatment of alcoholism with psychotomimetic drugs. A follow-up study. Activitas Nervosa Superior. 1978.
article.Title: Treatment of alcoholism with psychotomimetic drugs. A follow-up study

article.IsObservational: Retrospective/naturalistic follow-up of a clinical cohort: 31 men received a 'psycholytic cure' (LSD-25 then psilocybine) as ongoing clinical treatment since 1963, with outcomes assessed via case-record and inquiry analysis at an average 6-year follow-up. No randomization, no control/comparator arm, no experimental protocol described — coded as observational (case series with follow-up), not an RCT.
article.N: N=31 is the treated/analyzed cohort explicitly stated ('Thirty-one men... were the subjects'). The text later reports '18 patients (58%)' with satisfactory effect and 'the remaining 13 patients' — this is internally consistent (18+13=31, and 18/31=58.1%~58%), referring to the 13 patients without a satisfactory response, not a subtraction from the 18; no arithmetic inconsistency to flag.
article.PctFemale: Article states all 31 subjects were men ('Thirty-one men, age 23-62'); no female participants reported, so PctFemale=0 by direct statement rather than omission.
article.Substance: Text states LSD-25 was used from 1963-1969 and psilocybine (spelled 'psylocybine' in the original, an old-style spelling read through as unambiguous, not an OCR garble) thereafter, both within this same cohort's treatment history; both are listed per the comma-separation rule for multi-substance studies.
article.SafetyReported: The article (pages 81-82, the Rydzynski/Gruszczynski text only) contains no adverse-event, side-effect, complication, or safety-outcome reporting of any kind — it reports only abstinence/therapeutic-outcome rates and prognostic personality factors associated with response. The description of patients reacting to the 'psychotomimetic shock' with 'unpleasant feelings' is presented as a prognostic predictor of good treatment response, not as a harm/AE, and has no count or denominator, so it was not coded as an ae_events row.
article.AE_denominator: Per schema instruction, coded '.' (not 'NA') because SafetyReported='N' — no safety assessment population is defined.
article.Corpus/Prefix: No substance/condition grouping label evident in the text; coded '.'.
article.PctBIPOC: Not reported. Study conducted in Lodz, Poland (Institute of Mental Hygiene, Military Academy of Medicine); no race/ethnicity data given.
article.PctIndigenous: Not reported; no basis to estimate a value that must not exceed the also-unreported PctBIPOC.
article.Title: Used the title as printed in the article body itself (page 81: 'Treatment of alcoholism with psychotomimetic drugs. / A follow-up study'), which is legible and matches the given Citation, rather than the noisier OCR of the same title on the interlibrary-loan slip header (line 39: 'Treatment of alcoholisnn with psychotomimetic drugs A foiiow-up study').
article.OCR/document scope: This scanned file contains three distinct articles concatenated: (1) a fragment of a preceding, unrelated article on anticholinergic-poisoning treatment in animals (TA 03/atropine-type study, references list, ending in an address 'J.F., Hradec Kralove'), (2) the target Rydzynski & Gruszczynski alcoholism follow-up article (pp.81-82), and (3) a following, unrelated article by Bastecky/Podrouzek/Vinar on plasma-protein changes after lysergamide in healthy volunteers (a separate non-alcoholism, non-AE pharmacology study). Only article (2) was used for this extraction; (1) and (3) were identified as out-of-scope and excluded rather than treated as garbled continuations of the target article.
